content: Phenylephrine, mineral oil, and petrolatum should be applied externally to a cleansed hemorrhoidal area or to the lower portion of the anal canal. This application can be performed up to four times daily, particularly at night, in the morning, or after bowel movements that may aggravate hemorrhoids. For application to the lower anal canal, remove the cover from the dispensing cap and attach the cap to the tube. For intrarectal use, remove the cover from the applicator, attach the applicator to the ointment tube, and lubricate the applicator thoroughly. Gently insert the applicator into the rectum. After each use, clean the applicator and replace the cover. For children under 12 years of age, use is determined based on whether the benefits outweigh the risks. For individuals aged 12 years or older, the product can be applied externally to the cleansed hemorrhoidal area or lower anal canal up to four times daily, especially at night, in the morning, or after bowel movements that may worsen hemorrhoids. If using intrarectally, follow the same procedure of removing the applicator cover, attaching it to the ointment tube, lubricating the applicator, and gently inserting it into the rectum. Clean the applicator after each use and replace the cover. This product is for external use only. It contains phenylephrine, which is an alpha-adrenergic agonist that induces localized vasoconstriction and reduces inflammation. Mineral oil acts as an emollient, softening stool in the colon by slowing the absorption of fecal water. Petrolatum provides moisturizing and lubricating effects. Discontinue use and contact a physician if hemorrhoids worsen or do not improve within seven days, or if symptoms such as bleeding, redness, irritation, swelling, pain, or other adverse effects develop or increase. Do not exceed the recommended daily dose unless directed by a physician. Avoid inserting the product into the rectum using fingers, mechanical devices, or applicators. Keep this product out of the reach of children. If swallowed, seek medical help or contact a poison control center immediately. This product is generally considered safe for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. However, always consult a healthcare professional before use. Copyright © 2010 First DataBank, Inc.
